subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Solid vs. Liquid Fuel: Trade-Offs in Propulsion
description: One-minute skill: Solid vs. Liquid Fuel: Trade-Offs in Propulsion.

hook.text: Solid rockets are simple and powerful. Liquid rockets are efficient and controllable. Each has trade-offs the other doesn't.

buildup.text: Solid rockets mix fuel and oxidizer into a single grain. Once ignited, they burn until empty. There is no off switch.

discovery.text: Liquid rockets pump separate fuel and oxidizer into a combustion chamber. They can be throttled, shut down, and restarted.

twist.text: Hybrid rockets use solid fuel with liquid oxidizer. They combine the simplicity of solids with the control of liquids.

climax.text: SpaceShipOne used a hybrid motor burning rubber and nitrous oxide. It won the X Prize as the first private spacecraft.

punchline.text: Solids can't stop. Liquids are complex. Hybrids split the difference.

quiz.question: What is the main disadvantage of solid rocket motors?
options: They produce much less thrust than liquid-fueled engines of the same size
Once ignited they cannot be shut down, throttled, or restarted
Solid fuel is extremely expensive compared to liquid propellants
